Hi Alice —

Thanks — this is a good question and the right time to lock it down. Short answers up front: yes, we can issue separate invoices per tranche; VAT is applied at invoice-level according to the billing entity and place of supply; and we can route invoices to different Medicore entities, provided the order form / payment recipient fields are finalized before the first invoice.

Notes and clarifying items (to make sure legal and finance are aligned):
- Invoice cadence: Redwood can produce one invoice per tranche milestone (e.g., 200k on Q2 commencement, 200k on Q3, 200k on Q4). Each invoice will reference the order form and invoice number series.
- Entity routing: we need explicit invoice recipient data (entity name, VAT/Tax ID, remit address, and preferred billing email). If you want Q2 & Q3 to go to Medicore EU Ltd and Q4 to Medicore UK Ltd, please supply VAT IDs and PO remittance instructions for each.
- Tax treatment: VAT vs. reverse-charge — where Medicore is established in the EU and provides a valid VAT ID, we can issue a reverse-charge invoice (no VAT charged) if the place of supply rules apply. Otherwise Redwood will charge VAT on the invoice. For UK-entity invoices, UK VAT rules may apply.
- Withholding/tax gross-up: Redwood is not set up to withhold on behalf of customers. If your local rules require withholding, please confirm who bears the gross-up or whether Medicore will self-assess.

Action items for Medicore (please):
1) Confirm invoice recipient for each tranche with VAT/Tax IDs (one-liner with entity name + VAT ID is fine).
2) Confirm whether you require separate invoice PDFs for each legal entity or a single consolidated invoice with split remit lines.
3) If Medicore expects Redwood to accommodate any withholding, state the exact percent and whether you want gross-up language added to the order form.

Ben / Kim — tagging you for legal / billing ops input on two quick points: 1) do we need an order form exhibit documenting the tranche schedule and invoice numbers (we typically add Exhibit A), and 2) any redline required to support multi-entity invoice recipients?

Thanks,

Hi all —

Quick operational readout from finance/legal: we can support separate invoices per tranche and route them to different remit entities, but two items need to be explicit in the order form/appendix:
- Invoice recipient table (Exhibit A): columns = Tranche, Amount, Invoice recipient name, VAT/Tax ID, Remit email, Billing address. This prevents ambiguity at billing time.
- Billing credit and SLA credits: if you want invoices split across entities but prefer a single credit pool, we need a defined billing owner for crediting and dispute handling.

Tax specifics (high level):
- If Medicore provides an EU VAT ID for the EU invoices, we'll apply reverse charge and not collect VAT (customer self-accounting). Please attach the VAT cert for audit.
- For the UK tranche, we'll need UK VAT ID and will apply UK VAT where applicable.
- If your tax team requires Redwood to add "withholding gross-up" language, that's a commercial change and will need Legal sign-off; typically customer-side withholding is handled by the customer unless contractually agreed.

Kimberly — please confirm if Legal wants a redline to the MSA or if we can handle the invoice recipient table purely as an order form exhibit.
